summary: Granary Finance: streaming chunk drop + late-token accounting mismatch causing duplicate partial completions and billing delta
summary_brief: Customer observed repeated short streaming disconnects around 03:24-03:46 UTC that produced partial duplicate completions and a token accounting mismatch which inflated billed token counts. Major incident (P0) declared; mitigations applied and follow-up plan documented.
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 between ~03:24-03:46 UTC Granary Finance observed multiple user sessions where streaming responses were truncated then resumed producing duplicate partial completions. Downstream client reassembly created repeated token sequences and resulted in an apparent increase in billed tokens and unexpected repeated completions.

Impact: Multiple production customers under the Granary account reported increased token usage (up to 2.7x for some sessions) and duplicate outputs for conversational flows. Business impact: degraded user experience for core banking assistant flows and an invoice discrepancy flagged by the customer.

Environment: Hosted Redwood API (prod), region us-east-1, customer using enterprise workspace with model pin rwd-chat-3b and fallback redwood-quant-v1. Traffic passed through streaming-proxy pool sp-us-east-2 which had a recent kernel selection rollout.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start long-form chat session (prompt length ~600 tokens) over streaming endpoint.
2) At ~20-40s into generation, connection sees repeated small TCP retransmit spikes (network-level); streaming-proxy returns chunked frames with overlapping offsets.
3) Client replays or resumes and receives an overlapping chunk which the client app re-concatenates into the transcript, creating duplicated token subsequences.
4) Billing pipeline consumes chunk delimiter events and double-counts resumed token ranges when chunk offsets are non-monotonic.

Observed behavior: duplicate partial completions, non-monotonic streaming chunk offsets in proxy logs, and billing meter reports showing >100% token counts for affected sessions.

Expected behavior: streaming frames emitted with strictly increasing offsets; resumed frames should indicate resume tokens that prevent re-counting; billing pipeline should deduplicate resumed ranges.

Logs / evidence:
- Streaming-proxy logs (sp-us-east-2) show interleaved chunk IDs and offset regressions: sp-log-2026-03-10-03-26.gz (attached to ticket).
- Router trace: trace-id 0be7f330-us-east-03: shows fallback to quantized variant at 03:25:12 which coincided with increased prefix cache miss.
- Billing meter dump: billing-sample-granary-2026-03-10.csv shows token delta mismatch correlated to trace-ids.

Timeline (abridged):
- 03:22 UTC: first noisy-neighbor autoscale event in GPU pool gp-09 triggers brief kernel re-selection path.
- 03:24 UTC: customer reports first truncated stream via #support-escalations Slack.
- 03:26 UTC: SRE opens incident INC-2026-0310-71 and pages on-call.
- 03:30 UTC: mitigation: route Granary traffic to standby streaming-proxy pool sp-us-east-3; immediate reduction in truncations observed.
- 03:46 UTC: customer confirmed major reduction in duplicate outputs.
- 03:50 UTC: billing team started sample reconciliation; initial anomaly confirmed.

Mitigation applied: immediate routing to healthy streaming-proxy pool and temporary pinning of model variant to rwd-chat-3b (avoid fallback path). Short-term billing credit agreed and applied to affected invoice.

Root cause (summary): a combination of two factors: (1) an aggressive kernel-selection rollout introduced a short-lived code path in the streaming-proxy that emitted non-monotonic chunk offsets when an upstream runtime raced with the proxy's resume logic; (2) the billing ingestion service did not robustly deduplicate resumed token ranges when offsets decreased. The combination produced duplicated transcript segments and double-counted tokens.

Resolution/rollback: hotfix merged to streaming-proxy to enforce monotonic offsets and add a resume-marker header (PR github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/233). Billing ingestion patched to deduplicate by (trace-id, client-session, offset-range) and deployed to prod billing pipeline (PR github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/704). Post-deploy validation run 2026-03-12 passed with no further duplicate token events in sampled traffic.

Customer communication and outcome: Support and CS coordinated with Granary Finance (contacts: Lila Mercer, Head of Platform) — provided a timeline, an explanation of root cause, and a one-off invoice credit for the impacted billing period. Granary accepted the remediation and requested follow-up on monitoring and SLA guardrails.

Post-incident follow-up actions (work items):
- (A1) Add a streaming-chunk-monotonicity alert to prod observability (owner: Owen Park, due 2026-03-20).
- (A2) Add deduplication unit tests to billing ingestion and create a synthetic replay harness (owner: Samira Chen, due 2026-03-18).
- (A3) Add canary gating for kernel-selection rollouts that touch streaming-proxy resume logic (owner: Elena Kovalenko, due 2026-03-25).
- (A4) Run a 72-hour reconciliation job for billing using historical traces for Granary account and report variance (owner: Billing Ops, due 2026-03-17).
- (A5) Customer-facing post-incident summary and slide deck delivered to Granary (owner: CS - Maya Singh, delivered 2026-03-13).

Notes: This ticket consolidates the customer-facing summary, technical RCA, and the post-incident action tracker. Billing credit details are recorded in finance ticket FIN-4492 (internal).
resolution: Hotfix applied to streaming-proxy enforcing monotonic chunk offsets and billing ingestion deduplication deployed. One-off invoice credit issued to Granary Finance. Monitoring and canary processes updated. Ticket closed after customer sign-off.
